products.description:
Modern, driverless Windows printing — deployed through Intune without breaking production.

Microsoft is moving Windows printing off vendor drivers. Windows Ready Print is the modern driverless platform — Windows talks to printers over open standards (IPP, Mopria, eSCL, Universal Print) using the built-in Microsoft IPP Class Driver instead of an HP/Canon/Xerox/Ricoh/Brother .INF package. Windows Protected Print mode (WPP) on Windows 11 24H2 is the hardened form: it forces the PC to use Ready Print exclusively and blocks third-party drivers — closing the Print Spooler / Point-and-Print attack surface behind PrintNightmare.

The catch — and why an assessment comes first

Enabling WPP is not cosmetic. On an enabled device, printers using unsupported third-party drivers are removed, their drivers are pulled from the driver store, third-party Point and Print is blocked, some legacy software printers disappear, and some multifunction scanning stops unless the device supports Mopria/eSCL. And WPP is device-scoped — it affects every user on the PC. So enabling it fleet-wide without knowing what it will remove breaks printing in production. This solution finds what WPP would remove before it removes it.

Run it as a project — assessment through hardening

Self-guided, click-by-click documentation plus five PowerShell tools and a clear engineer-led runbook.

  • Assess — inventory every driver and printer; classify each as Ready-Print eligible, needs Universal Print, or a blocker (non-Mopria, legacy software printer, eSCL-less scanner).
  • Design the target path — direct IPP/Mopria and/or Universal Print — and set the WPP scope.
  • Configure the Intune Custom OMA-URI profile (the setting is not yet in the Settings Catalog): ConfigureWindowsProtectedPrint = <enabled/>, scoped to 24H2+ devices.
  • Pilot & validate, migrate off legacy print servers/Point-and-Print, then roll out in rings and prevent regression.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview, Requirements, the Phase 1–7 Deployment Strategy, Testing, Troubleshooting, and Best Practices — every object named, with a GCC High note.
  • Five PowerShell tools: Get-PrintDriverInventory (third-party vs IPP-class), Test-MopriaReadiness (IPP/IPPS), Test-ScanCapability (eSCL), Get-WPPState (24H2 eligibility + state), and Validate-Deployment.

The bottom line

A hardened, driverless print estate on Windows 11 — reduced attack surface, fewer update-driven print outages, and alignment with Microsoft's V3/V4 driver end-of-servicing — deployed on evidence, with the printers WPP would remove found first. One fixed price; re-run the assessment and validation as your fleet evolves. Downloadable guide plus scripts.
